H('IV. Governing Legal Framework (Summary)', 1)
P('**Stark Law.** Absent an applicable exception, a physician may not refer a Medicare patient for DHS to an entity with which the physician (or an immediate family member) has a financial relationship. The entity may not bill Medicare for DHS furnished on a prohibited referral (42 U.S.C. § 1395nn(a)(1); 42 C.F.R. § 411.353). Clinical laboratory and radiology/imaging services are DHS. Services paid as part of the ASC composite rate are excluded from DHS (42 C.F.R. § 411.351, definition of “designated health services”). A “referral” includes a request for a consultation with another physician and any test or procedure ordered by that consultant (§ 411.351). The statute imposes strict liability. The sanctions are:')
B('denial of payment and an obligation to refund (§ 1395nn(g)(1)–(2));')
B('civil monetary penalties per service billed with knowledge, and per circumvention scheme (§ 1395nn(g)(3)–(4)), as inflation-adjusted under 45 C.F.R. Part 102;')
B('exclusion.')
P('The Medicaid analogue is 42 U.S.C. § 1396b(s). Since the CMS final rule effective January 19, 2021, compensation “takes into account” the volume or value of referrals only if the formula uses referrals as a variable and the compensation rises or falls with them (§ 411.354(d)(5)–(6)). A per-referral payment is the paradigm case.')
P('**Group practice and IOASE.** The IOASE (§ 411.355(b)) protects both ownership and compensation relationships for in-office DHS. It is available only if Greenfield qualifies as a “group practice” under § 411.352. Among other requirements:')
B('the members of the group, taken in the aggregate, must furnish at least 75% of their total patient care services through the group (§ 411.352(d));')
B('no physician who is a member of the group may receive compensation directly or indirectly based on the volume or value of his or her DHS referrals, except through a profit share or productivity bonus that meets § 411.352(i) (§ 411.352(g)).')
P('“Members of the group” are owners and employees. Independent contractors are not members; they may be “physicians in the group practice” (§ 411.351). The IOASE also requires that the DHS be:')
B('furnished personally by the referring physician or a group member, or by individuals supervised in accordance with applicable Medicare payment and coverage rules (§ 411.355(b)(1));')

P('**Other relevant Stark exceptions.**')
B('Bona fide employment, § 411.357(c): identifiable services; FMV; not determined in any manner that takes into account the volume or value of referrals; commercially reasonable. Claims “resulting from” an AKS violation are false under the FCA (42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b(g)). Circuits are split on the causation standard for AKS-tainted claims, and the current Sixth Circuit position should be confirmed. Stark-tainted claims are false without any intent showing for the underlying violation, but FCA liability requires that the claims be submitted “knowingly” (31 U.S.C. § 3729(b)(1)). P('The audit memo and Manual §§ 3.2.5 and 5.4 **misstate the law**, and the misstatement cuts both ways.')

It is not a per-physician threshold, and IC physicians are not “members of the group” (§ 411.351). The four ICs’ 60% share therefore does not by itself defeat group-practice status. On the audit’s data (52 members assumed at the threshold; 31 of 35 employees at or above 75%; 4 employees at about 50%), the aggregate test appears satisfied, subject to verification.')
B('**The real risks lie elsewhere.**')
B('(i) **IOASE furnishing element.** ICs may be “physicians in the group practice” only for the time they furnish services to group patients in the group’s facilities under a contractual arrangement (§ 411.351). Whether a professional component personally performed by a non-member IC, particularly one read remotely, fits § 411.355(b)(1) and the location requirements requires analysis. Off-site teleradiology reads are the most exposed.', 1)
B('(ii) **Anti-markup rule.** For diagnostic tests billed by a supplier that did not perform them, payment is limited unless the performing physician “shares a practice” with the billing supplier. That requires furnishing substantially all (75%) of professional services through the billing group, or meeting the site-of-service test (42 C.F.R. § 414.50). At 60%, the ICs likely fail the substantially-all prong, so the site-of-service analysis is critical. Overbilling under the anti-markup rule is an overpayment independent of Stark.', 1)
B('(iii) **Reassignment.** Each IC’s reassignment of benefits must be valid (CMS-855R; 42 C.F.R. § 424.80), with joint and several liability language and records access.', 1)
H('Remediation', 3)
N('Obtain the four IC agreements, CMS-855R reassignments, read-location logs and billing data. Determine where each professional component was performed.')
N('Prospectively, either employ the radiologists, or bill their off-site reads in compliance with the anti-markup rule, or have them bill directly.')
N('Correct Manual §§ 3.2.5 and 5.4 and train billing staff on the correct tests.')
N('Quantify any anti-markup or IOASE overpayment for the disclosure analysis.')
